title: NBA Daily Digest: Offseason Heats Up with Major Signings and Trades
subtitle: Friday, August 21, 2026

items.headline: James Harden Inks Three-Year, $97M Deal to Return to Cleveland Cavaliers
items.summary: Eleven-time All-Star James Harden has agreed to a new three-year, $97 million contract to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers. Harden, who declined a $42.3 million player option earlier this summer, secures the long-term security he sought. This move follows a multi-team trade that reshaped the Cavs' backcourt.

items.headline: Cavaliers Acquire Peyton Watson in Five-Team Blockbuster Deal
items.summary: In a complex five-team trade, the Cleveland Cavaliers have acquired wing Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets. The deal, reported on Wednesday, also saw Max Strus move to the LA Clippers, while the Cavs also landed Cam Whitmore from WAS. Denver received a 2031 unprotected first-round pick and a 2032 second-round pick, among other assets.

items.headline: Harden's $97M Deal Puts Him Among NBA's Elite Earners
items.summary: James Harden's new three-year, $97 million contract with the Cavaliers projects his career earnings to surpass $511 million, making him only the fourth player in NBA history to cross the $500 million mark, joining LeBron James, Kevin Durant, and Stephen Curry. The deal includes a player option for the 2028-29 season.

items.headline: LeBron James Joins Philadelphia 76ers in Marquee Offseason Move
items.summary: Earlier this offseason, four-time MVP LeBron James made headlines by signing with the Philadelphia 76ers for his 24th NBA season, closing one of the summer's biggest free agency sagas. His arrival, alongside earlier acquisition Jaylen Brown, has transformed the Sixers into championship contenders.

items.headline: Other Notable Free Agency Updates Across the League
items.summary: The Boston Celtics secured center Mitchell Robinson on a three-year, $47M+ deal, strengthening their frontcourt after losing Kristaps Porzingis. Restricted free agent Jalen Duren's contract standoff with the DET Pistons continues, though he is expected to return to the team for the 2026-27 season.

items.headline: Five-Team Deal Sends Peyton Watson to Cavs, Max Strus to Clippers
items.summary: The complex multi-team trade saw Peyton Watson depart the DEN Nuggets for the CLE Cavaliers. The LA Clippers acquired Max Strus, while the Washington Wizards received Tre Mann, a 2027 second-round pick, and cash. Cleveland also landed Cam Whitmore, and Denver received Julian Reese, an unprotected 2031 first-round pick, and a 2032 second-round pick.

items.headline: Coaching Carousel Continues: Key Hires and Staff Changes
items.summary: Several coaching changes have taken place this offseason. Tiago Splitter was named Head Coach of the CHI Bulls, Dusty May took the helm for the DAL Mavericks, and Taylor Jenkins joined the MIL Bucks. Jamahl Mosley moved from Orlando to become the new Head Coach of the NOP Pelicans.

items.headline: 2026-27 NBA Season Schedule Revealed, Highlighted by LeBron's Sixers Debut
items.summary: The NBA officially released its schedule for the 2026-27 season, set to tip off on October 20. Key matchups include LeBron James' debut with the PHI 76ers, and international games in Paris and Manchester. The schedule also features a four-game slate on Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

items.headline: Russell Westbrook Announces Retirement After 18 Seasons
items.summary: Veteran guard and former MVP Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from professional basketball on August 12, 2026, concluding an 18-season NBA career that included an MVP award in 2017 and an NBA Finals appearance in 2012 with the OKC Thunder.
